response.answer: The map does not contain high school graduation rates, so I used the closest available measure: the share of adults 25+ without a high school diploma (a different measure, not the same as graduation rates). By that measure, the ZIPs with the highest shares lacking a diploma are: 33493 (Palm Beach County) at 41.3%, 33030 (Miami-Dade) at 39.4%, 33128 (Miami-Dade) at 36.7%, 33034 (Miami-Dade) at 35.7%, 33142 (Miami-Dade) at 35.6%, 33430 (Palm Beach) at 32.9%, 33010 (Miami-Dade) at 32.5%, 33476 (Palm Beach) at 31.8%, 33127 (Miami-Dade) at 31.7%, and 33125 (Miami-Dade) at 31.6%. Of these, 33493, 33030, 33034, 33142, 33430, and 33127 also fall in the high educational-need tier, and 33127 and 33430 have the highest composite need scores. 165 ZIPs have this measure; the top 10 are shown.
response.interpretation: No graduation-rate data exists in this map. Read the question as asking which ZIPs have the lowest educational attainment, measured by share of adults without a high school diploma.
assumptions: "High need" means the top third of reliable ZIPs in Miami Metro by composite educational-need score (40% Haitian-ancestry share, 30% households without internet, 30% adults without a high school diploma): score ≥ 60.5 is high, 36.4–60.5 medium, below 36.4 low.
16 ZIPs in scope were excluded because they have too few residents for reliable estimates.
Figures are ACS 2022 5-year estimates, which carry margins of error.
